entries.reason: the method is deprecated by the SDK and rightly so: TLS cannot be taken off a connection that has it, and on a connection that never started it there is nothing to stop. There is no state to change on either side of the call
entries.effect: nothing happens, and the method says so once in the log the first time it is used, which is what the status requires
entries.source: SDK 26.2 headers, whose own deprecation text is the reason; the port's own TLS ask, in -startSecureConnection

entries.reason: the port makes this call on the session's delegate; the method itself is the application's and the port defines none, so what is carried is the call and not an implementation of the selector. The call is in facts/Foundation/NSURLSessionStreamTask.md and on the device
entries.effect: the method is the delegate's own, so a subclass of the protocol implements it and the port's library carries no such selector

entries.effect: the method is not there: respondsToSelector: answers honestly and an unchecked call raises

entries.reason: the SDK's own header deprecates -init and +new in favour of the two factories, and a deprecation is a warning rather than a refusal: the port answers -init, which is what the release's own -[NSURLSessionTask init] does
